title: 硬件加速、RenderThread、GPU 内存与 dma-buf
key_conclusions: Graphics memory growth must be attributed across UI thread, RenderThread, HWUI/Skia, GPU driver, gralloc, dma-buf, and SurfaceFlinger.
Java Heap and Native Heap can stay stable while hardware Bitmap, texture, layer, or Surface buffers increase Graphics memory.
dma-buf ownership requires producer-consumer evidence; process-local PSS does not prove who must release a shared buffer.
Validation requires before/after meminfo Graphics, fd/dma-buf evidence, SurfaceFlinger state, lifecycle release, and workload replay.
shallow_points: The article does not include real SurfaceFlinger dumps, fd listings, dmabuf data, or Perfetto render traces.
It does not validate vendor GPU driver visibility or debugfs permissions across devices and ROMs.
It does not provide runnable TextureView, SurfaceView, hardware Bitmap, or layer leak samples.
It does not quantify texture cache, layer cache, or upload costs on target hardware.
